name: CA-15
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+26 partisan lean makes the district deeply Democratic
Incumbent Kevin Mullin holds a large fundraising edge; the challenger shows no reported money
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent
No public polling or expert ratings; the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing
model.rationale: A 26-point Democratic district, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with no visible fundraising leave little room for competition, and markets price Mullin's win odds near 97 percent. The forecast stays at Safe D with an expected margin in the high twenties.
model.watch: With no polling coverage, a late scandal, a sudden influx of challenger or outside spending, or unusual turnout dynamics are the main things that could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 15th District sits deep in Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 26 points toward the party. Kevin Mullin, the incumbent Democrat, is running for re-election and has built a substantial financial lead, raising about $820,000 while holding more than $200,000 on hand. His Republican challenger, Charles Hoelter, shows no reported fundraising, leaving him with little visible campaign infrastructure in a district that favors the other party by a wide margin.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put Mullin's chances near 97 percent. The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate, an established incumbent, and a largely invisible challenger campaign makes this one of the safest Democratic holds on the House map, with the main open question being the size of the winning margin rather than the winner.
